blocking.title: pr-gate SHA check reads FETCH_HEAD, which resolves to main rather than the PR head, so reviewers stop on a false mismatch and skeptics refute by default
blocking.failurePath:
Input: any PR. READ_RULES tells every reviewer and skeptic to run `git fetch origin main pull/${pr}/head` and then check `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` == headSha. When two refspecs are given on the command line, both are written for-merge and FETCH_HEAD resolves to the FIRST line, which is origin main. In this run, `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` printed 89cc02920435933dfbc438b12079cb13c836ad24 (main), not b67e340. The rule then says 'report the SHA you saw as headSha and stop'.

Wrong results:
(a) Reviewers that follow it literally return main's SHA with empty findings. shaMismatch is non-empty and go=false for every PR, however correct the PR is. The gate cannot pass.
(b) Fail-open mix: the skeptic prompt reuses READ_RULES but SKEPTIC_SCHEMA has no headSha field, and the skeptic is told 'If you cannot confirm it, set refuted to true'. A skeptic that stops on the false mismatch therefore refutes. If the reviewers worked around the check (reported the right SHA and a real blocking finding) but both skeptics stop literally, the finding is dropped as 'refuted' (line 137) and go can be true.

Fix: fetch the head into a named ref (`git fetch origin main pull/${pr}/head:refs/pr-gate/${pr}`) and compare `git rev-parse refs/pr-gate/${pr}`, or list pull/${pr}/head first. The same fetch line at :64 is unaffected because it checks out ${headSha} directly.
blocking.evidence:
cat .git/FETCH_HEAD after the prescribed fetch:
89cc0292...		branch 'main' of https://github.com/xiechimon/pacman
b67e340f...		'refs/pull/1410/head' of ...
`git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` -> 89cc02920435933dfbc438b12079cb13c836ad24
skeptics:
I confirmed the finding at b67e340fe889608ae9bebc6767d07e70b6bbb6ab; it is real.

1. Line 36 of .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js tells every reviewer and skeptic to run `git fetch origin main pull/${pr}/head` and then check that `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` equals headSha. I ran that exact fetch (git 2.43.0). FETCH_HEAD had two lines, main (89cc02920435933dfbc438b12079cb13c836ad24) first and refs/pull/1410/head (b67e340f...) second. `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` printed 89cc0292..., which is main. Running the fetch again with pull/1410/head listed first made `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` print b67e340f..., so the refspec order causes the mismatch. The PR head itself is correct: the REST API returns head.sha b67e340f.

2. Path (a), fail closed: a reviewer that follows line 36 literally reports headSha=89cc0292... with no findings. Lines 152-154 then put that reviewer in shaMismatch, and line 174 sets go=false. If reviewers follow the rule, no PR can pass the gate.

3. Path (b), fail open: line 128 builds the skeptic prompt from READ_RULES and adds "If you cannot confirm it, set refuted to true". SKEPTIC_SCHEMA (lines 93-100) has no headSha field, so a skeptic that stops on the false mismatch can only say refuted=true. At line 133 `confirmed` is then empty, and line 137 logs the finding as refuted and drops it. If the reviewers worked around the check and reported the right SHA, go can be true while a real blocking finding has been thrown away. This prompt is itself a skeptic prompt built that way, and following its fetch rule literally would have stopped me.

4. Line 64 (the evidence dimension) is not affected, because it runs `git checkout --detach ${headSha}` and does not read FETCH_HEAD.

The fix the reviewer proposed works. Either fetch the PR head into a named ref and compare that ref, or list pull/${pr}/head before main.

I could not refute it; the failure reproduces at b67e340. Line 36 of `.claude/workflows/pr-gate.js` (READ_RULES) tells every reviewer and skeptic to run `git fetch origin main pull/${pr}/head` and then check that `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` equals headSha. I ran that exact fetch with git 2.43.0. `.git/FETCH_HEAD` then held two lines, both for-merge: first 89cc0292... "branch 'main'", then b67e340f... "'refs/pull/1410/head'". `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` returns the first line, 89cc02920435933dfbc438b12079cb13c836ad24. That is `git rev-parse origin/main`, not the PR head. The REST API confirms the PR head is b67e340fe889608ae9bebc6767d07e70b6bbb6ab.

So the check fails for every PR, and the rule's literal next step ("report the SHA you saw as headSha and stop") sends main's SHA back as headSha. REVIEW_RULES includes READ_RULES (line 41), so all five dimensions get this step, the evidence dimension too. Lines 152-154 turn any reported headSha that differs from args.headSha into a shaMismatch entry, and line 174 then sets go=false. A gate whose reviewers follow the instructions can never pass.

The skeptic prompt (line 128) reuses READ_RULES, but SKEPTIC_SCHEMA (lines 93-100) has no headSha field. The prompt also says "If you cannot confirm it, set refuted to true". A skeptic that stops on the false mismatch therefore votes refuted. When both skeptics do that, lines 133-137 drop a real blocking finding as "refuted", so the gate can wrongly pass when the reviewers worked around the check but the skeptics did not.

The one path that avoids FETCH_HEAD is the evidence prompt's own `git checkout --detach ${headSha}` at line 64. It does not override the READ_RULES check above it. The suggested fix works: fetch the head into a named ref, or list pull/N/head first, and compare against that.

blocking.title: Skeptic agents that return null count as refutations, so a blocking finding can disappear and the gate says go
blocking.failurePath:
State: a reviewer reports blocking finding F. Both skeptic agent() calls in the parallel() resolve to null, which the workflow API returns when the user skips an agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries.

Trace: `votes.filter(Boolean)` is [], so `confirmed.length` is 0. F takes the else branch and is logged as `refuted (dim): F.title` (line 137). It is pushed to neither blocking nor unrefuted. If the other reviews are present with the right SHA, `go` is true (line 172) and the caller enables auto-merge with an unadjudicated blocking finding.

The same happens for one null plus one refute: one refutation of two is not the majority that spec 28 §7.5 (line 246) requires ('多数反驳即撤销'). The cap path at :115-118 already fails closed; the null path should too. Count refutations explicitly, e.g. drop F only when `votes.filter(v => v && v.refuted).length === 2`, and keep F (or add it to missing) when any vote is null.
blocking.evidence:
const confirmed = votes.filter(Boolean).filter((v) => !v.refuted)
if (confirmed.length >= 1) { blocking.push(...) } else { log(`refuted (${d.key}): ${f.title}`) }

blocking.title: pr-gate step 1 compares the head SHA against FETCH_HEAD, which resolves to origin/main, so the ticket item 'pr-gate 可按名调用' fails as written and the PR shows no evidence for it
blocking.failurePath: Every reviewer is told to run `git fetch origin main pull/${pr}/head` and then confirm that `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` equals headSha. Git writes one FETCH_HEAD line per fetched ref in command-line order, so main comes first, and `rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` resolves to the first line. On this PR the command printed 89cc02920435933dfbc438b12079cb13c836ad24 (origin/main), not b67e340. The prompt then says to 'report the SHA you saw as headSha and stop'. A reviewer that does this returns headSha=89cc029. Lines 152-154 put it in shaMismatch, and line 174 makes go=false for every PR. The gate can never return go while reviewers follow it literally. Ticket #1401's acceptance item '`pr-gate` workflow 存仓，可按名调用' is the only scope item that is executable code. The PR's Acceptance section does not list it, the Verified section never mentions pr-gate.js or a run of it, and the PR still closes #1401.
blocking.evidence: Reproduced in this review. `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` gave 89cc029. The FETCH_HEAD file contains `89cc029... branch 'main'` followed by `b67e340... 'refs/pull/1410/head'`. pr-gate.js:36 is the instruction, :152-154 build shaMismatch, :174 sets go. Ticket #1401's acceptance list includes the pr-gate item, and the PR body's Acceptance section has only three items, none about pr-gate. A fix is to compare against `git rev-parse refs/pull/...` fetched into a named ref, or against `git rev-parse ${headSha}^{commit}` after the fetch.
skeptics:
I reproduced the failure at b67e340fe889608ae9bebc6767d07e70b6bbb6ab. Running `git fetch origin main pull/1410/head` wrote FETCH_HEAD with `89cc02920435933dfbc438b12079cb13c836ad24 branch 'main'` on line 1 and `b67e340... 'refs/pull/1410/head'` on line 2. Neither line is marked not-for-merge. `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` returned 89cc029, which is origin/main, not the PR head.

The code at b67e340 carries the instruction into the verdict:
- `.claude/workflows/pr-gate.js:36` (READ_RULES) tells every reviewer to run that fetch, compare `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` with headSha, and if they differ, "report the SHA you saw as headSha and stop".
- READ_RULES is in every reviewer prompt (REVIEW_RULES, :41) and every skeptic prompt (:128).
- FINDINGS_SCHEMA requires `headSha` (:71, :90).
- A reviewer that follows the instruction returns headSha=89cc029. Lines 152-154 put that dimension in `shaMismatch`, and line 174 sets `go` to false whenever `shaMismatch` is non-empty.

On every open PR whose head differs from main, the gate therefore returns go=false whenever a reviewer follows the instruction as written. Whether a given run fails depends on whether a reviewer notices the mistake and ignores the instruction. The instruction itself is wrong every time.

The evidence gap is also confirmed:
- Ticket #1401's acceptance list includes "`pr-gate` workflow 存仓，可按名调用".
- The PR body's Acceptance section has only three items, none about pr-gate.
- The Verified section's diff stat lists only three docs files and says "No product code changes" and "the diff touches three markdown files and no code, config or workflow file".
- The real `git diff --stat origin/main...b67e340` shows five files, including `.claude/workflows/pr-gate.js` (182 lines) and `.gitignore`.
- The PR says "Closes #1401".

Fix: fetch the PR into a named ref (e.g. `git fetch origin pull/${pr}/head:refs/remotes/pr/${pr}`) and compare against that, or compare `git rev-parse ${headSha}^{commit}`. Either way, put pull/N/head first or alone in the fetch.

I confirmed the failure at b67e340. I ran the exact command from pr-gate.js:36 (`git fetch origin main pull/1410/head`) on git 2.43.0. FETCH_HEAD then held two lines: `89cc02920435933dfbc438b12079cb13c836ad24 branch 'main'` first and `b67e340fe889608ae9bebc6767d07e70b6bbb6ab 'refs/pull/1410/head'` second. Neither line is marked not-for-merge, and `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD` printed 89cc029 (origin/main). It reads the first line, and git writes FETCH_HEAD in refspec order, so `main` is always first.

The READ_RULES text at :36 tells every reviewer and skeptic to confirm that this value equals headSha, and otherwise to "report the SHA you saw as headSha and stop". A reviewer that follows this literally returns headSha=89cc029. Lines 152-154 add any review whose headSha differs from args.headSha to shaMismatch, and line 174 then sets go=false. This happens for every PR, because the check compares main against the PR head, so a literal run of the gate can never return go. The workaround I used (`git rev-parse b67e340^{commit}` after the fetch) resolves correctly. The evidence dimension's own checkout of headSha works, but it gets the same READ_RULES and the same check.

The documentation side also holds. Ticket #1401's acceptance list includes "`pr-gate` workflow 存仓，可按名调用", and the PR's Acceptance section ticks only three items, none of them pr-gate. The Verified section claims the branch diff is "the three documents" and shows a 3-file --stat. The real diff `git diff --stat origin/main...b67e340` has 5 files: .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js (+182), .gitignore, and the three docs, so that claim is stale. The Risk section says "no code, config or workflow file", which is false at the head. The PR body still says "Closes #1401".

One judgment call: "可按名调用" could be read narrowly as "the file exists with meta.name 'pr-gate'". Even so, the concrete failure path in pr-gate.js:36 → :152-154 → :174 is real.

blocking.title: pr-gate drops a blocking finding when its skeptic agents fail (null), which fails open and contradicts spec 28 §7.5's 'majority refute withdraws'; no test or failure-mode list covers it
blocking.failurePath: A reviewer reports a real blocking finding, and both skeptic agents return null (crash, timeout or schema failure). The code expects null votes: `votes.filter(Boolean)` at :133. confirmed.length is 0, so the else branch at :136-137 logs 'refuted' and discards the finding. If nothing else blocks, go is true at :174 and the caller enables auto-merge (spec 28 l.246, l.254). With one skeptic refuting and one null, the finding is also dropped. Spec 28 §7.5 l.246 says 多数反驳即撤销 (withdraw on majority refutation), and 1 of 2 or 0 of 2 refutations is not a majority. Spec 28 P3's matching failure mode, 三视角之一超时 → 不合成 go (a timeout must not produce go), is also violated in spirit. The other agent-failure paths fail closed: a null review counts as missing (:149-151), and over-cap findings are kept (:118-121). This is the only path where an agent failure turns into go. Ticket #1401 puts pr-gate in scope but lists no pr-gate failure modes, and the head has no test for the gate's aggregation logic.
blocking.evidence: pr-gate.js:124-138, the skeptic loop. :133 `const confirmed = votes.filter(Boolean).filter((v) => !v.refuted)`. :134-138 keep the finding only if confirmed.length >= 1, otherwise log it as refuted. docs/spec/28 l.246: '每条 blocking 发现派 2 个反驳者（默认判「不成立」，多数反驳即撤销）'. A fix that matches the spec: drop the finding only when the count of non-null votes with refuted === true is 2.

blocking.title: Skeptic failures silently drop blocking findings (gate fails open)
blocking.failurePath: A reviewer returns a blocking finding. Both skeptic agent() calls in the parallel() at lines 124-132 come back null. Under the Workflow runtime this happens when a subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries, when the user skips it, or when agent() throws because the turn's token budget is spent (parallel() turns a throwing thunk into null and never rejects). Line 133 computes `confirmed = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted)` = []. The else branch at line 137 logs `refuted (...)` and the finding never reaches `blocking`. `go` (line 171) is then true if nothing else blocks, and per spec 28 §7.4/§7.5 the main session enables auto-merge for non-protected PRs. A mixed result [null, {refuted:true}] also drops the finding on a single refutation, although spec 28 §7.5 (docs/spec/28 line 246) says a finding is withdrawn only when a majority of refuters agree. This is the opposite of the reviewer path: a dead reviewer becomes `missing` and forces go=false (fail-closed). A dead skeptic instead erases the finding (fail-open).
blocking.evidence: pr-gate.js:133-138 `const confirmed = votes.filter(Boolean).filter((v) => !v.refuted); if (confirmed.length >= 1) { blocking.push(...) } else { log(`refuted (${d.key}): ${f.title}`) }`. A fix is to count refutations instead (`votes.filter(v => v && v.refuted).length >= 2` withdraws) and keep the finding marked 'skeptics: failed' when a vote is null, as the cap branch at lines 118-121 already does.

blocking.title: Verified section's git diff --stat output does not reproduce at head; body predates commit b67e340
blocking.failurePath: I ran the quoted command `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` with HEAD = b67e340. It lists 5 files and 532 insertions: .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js (+182), .gitignore (+1), ADR 0018 (+2), ADR 0021 (+73) and spec 28 (+274). The PR body pastes 3 files and 349 insertions. That pasted output matches the parent 0b67ca9 (3 files, 349 insertions). The PR was created at 20:27:49Z and b67e340 was pushed at 20:30:46Z without a body update. Other claims in the body are also false at the head. Risk says "the diff touches three markdown files and no code, config or workflow file". What says "No product code changes" and lists three documents. At the head, the diff adds a JavaScript workflow script and a .gitignore rule. A reviewer or merger who trusts the body would approve a change whose scope the body misstates. That scope includes a D4 protected path, .claude/workflows/** per spec 28 §7.5.
blocking.evidence: Head: ` 5 files changed, 532 insertions(+)`. `git diff --stat origin/main...0b67ca9` gives ` 3 files changed, 349 insertions(+)`. `git show --stat b67e340` lists .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js | 182, .gitignore | 1, and spec 28 | 2 +-.

suggestions.title: Routing to the user (mergedBy) depends only on the LLM listing D4 paths; there is no deterministic match
suggestions.failurePath:
mergedBy is 'auto-merge' whenever no reviewer fills protectedPaths. Suppose the safety reviewer leaves out a changed file that matches D4, e.g. it misses `scripts/foo-gate.mjs` or treats `.claude/workflows/pr-gate.js` as out of scope. go=true and mergedBy='auto-merge' then route a protected change to auto-merge, against ADR 0021 D4 and spec 28 D7.

The script cannot run git, but it can ask the safety agent for the full `git diff --name-only origin/main...headSha` list in a separate field and do the D4 glob match in script code, so the routing is deterministic.

suggestions.title: Parallel reviewers run `git fetch origin main` in the same shared clone and can collide on the ref lock
suggestions.failurePath:
Up to min(16, CPUs-2) reviewers or skeptics, plus the worktree agent (worktrees share refs), run `git fetch origin main ...` at the same time. Two fetches updating refs/remotes/origin/main at once can fail with 'cannot lock ref ... main.lock: File exists', and both overwrite the shared FETCH_HEAD.

An agent that does not retry may report an error or stop, which surfaces as missing or a false shaMismatch (fail-closed). Consider fetching once before the fan-out (by the caller) and having the agents only `git cat-file -e ${headSha}`.

suggestions.title: ADR 0021 D3: 'update-branch keeps the digest unchanged' holds only in a narrower case
suggestions.file: docs/adr/0021-自治合并-项目级策略与补丁绑定判定.md
suggestions.failurePath:
The digest is sha256 over `status filename blobSha` from compare/{base}...{headSha}, and compare `files[].sha` is the blob at head.

Case 1: main changed a file the PR also changes. After update-branch, that file's blob at the new head includes main's hunks, so its blobSha and the digest change, and the verdict is forced to re-run. The claim also appears at spec 28 line 70.
Case 2: P3 pins `base` to the PR's recorded base.sha instead of the moving branch name. After update-branch, the three-dot merge base is still the old SHA, so all of main's merged-in files enter the list and every update-branch invalidates the verdict.

Both cases fail safe (an extra re-verify), but the stated invariant is false as written. State the condition (base = branch name, no file overlap with the commits merged in) so the P3 tests are not written against a false invariant.

suggestions.title: ADR 0021 D2 and spec 28 D2 call lib/github.ts the only github.com egress; skill-import.ts also calls api.github.com
suggestions.file: docs/adr/0021-自治合并-项目级策略与补丁绑定判定.md
suggestions.failurePath: At the head, apps/server/src/services/skill-import.ts:89 defines `GH_API_BASE = 'https://api.github.com'` and fetches repos/{o}/{r} and git/trees directly (lines 405, 441, 476, 487), bypassing lib/github.ts. These are reads, but a P2/P4 audit that relies on 'single egress' (for example, grep lib/github.ts to prove that merge is the only new write) would rest on a false premise. Say 'the only github.com write egress', or note the skill-import read path.

suggestions.title: Three branch commits break the <scope>(<ticket>): <subject> format, and the AGENTS.md squash procedure would land one of them on main
suggestions.failurePath: The subjects of ca088ce, 3944905 and 662cbd9 have no ticket. Each is `docs: spec 28 ...` without (1401), against AGENTS.md:61. The squash recipe at AGENTS.md:70 is `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/1410/commits -q '.[0].commit.message'`. For this PR that returns ca088ce: subject `docs: spec 28 自举闭环计划（pacman 自写 PR、自合 PR，goal 模式执行）` with no ticket, and a body with no `closes #1401` line. A merger who follows the recipe therefore lands a non-conforming subject on main and drops the closing line that the PR body says comes from e5414a2. AGENTS.md:63 also says the PR-body `Closes #1401` does not reach the commit, so #1401 can stay OPEN. GitHub's default squash avoids this: per repo settings it uses the PR title `docs(1401): ...` plus every commit message, so `closes #1401` from e5414a2 is included. Rewording the commits would need a force push, which AGENTS.md forbids. Fix at merge time: use the PR title as the subject and make sure the body ends with `closes #1401`.

suggestions.title: Spec 28 §7.5 and §8 disagree with the pr-gate.js this PR ships
suggestions.failurePath:
Commit b67e340 says it wrote the real path and args into §7.5, but other parts of §7.5 and §8 no longer match the script.
- Output shape: the §7.5 table row (line 246) gives pr-gate's output as `{headSha, go, blocking[], notes}`. pr-gate.js:170-182 returns {pr, ticket, headSha, go, blocking, suggestions, protectedPaths, mergedBy, missing, shaMismatch, checked}, with no `notes`.
- Evidence dimension: the row says it re-runs the matching verify-pacman driver at headSha. pr-gate.js:64 instead re-runs at most three of the narrowest commands quoted in the PR's Verified section.
- Rules dimension: the row says it covers docs/pr-review.md and the attribution trailers (尾标). pr-gate.js:51 mentions neither.
- Skeptic cap: when the cap is reached, pr-gate.js:118-121 keeps blocking findings without any skeptics. The spec does not document this.
- §8 P0 row (line 264): the PR column says `见 #1401 的关联 PR` instead of #1410, but the ledger rule at line 226 says to fill in the PR number after opening. Its evidence column says `不适用（仅文档）`, but P0 now ships an executable workflow script.

A later session that resumes from the spec after context compaction (which §8 names as the only source of truth for progress) will expect `notes` and verify-pacman reruns that the gate does not produce.

suggestions.title: Spec 28 P5 and ADR 0021 D2 assume only the server-composed message reaches main, which conflicts with the AGENTS.md squash rule on the human path
suggestions.failurePath:
Spec 28 line 140 keeps daemon in-branch commits in `<kind>: <title>` form. Its reasoning is that after a squash only the message the server builds under D2 reaches main. ADR 0021 D2 (adr line 35) has the server take the title from the PR title.

But the default policy is `mergePolicy = human`, and under it a human can still merge on GitHub using the AGENTS.md:70 recipe, which takes `.[0].commit.message`. That is the daemon's first `<kind>: <title>` commit, so a subject without a ticket and without `closes #N` lands on main (the same path as finding 1).

D2's PR-title-as-subject rule also differs from AGENTS.md:70, which takes the subject from the commit message. Fix, when P2 or P4 lands: update AGENTS.md:70 to match D2, or have daemon commitAll write the `<scope>(<ticket>)` form. AGENTS.md is a D4 protected path, so that change goes through the user.
